The World Bank Group has launched its first comprehensive digital strategy, placing artificial intelligence, affordable internet access and job creation at the centre of its development agenda as 1.2 billion young people prepare to enter the workforce in developing countries over the next 10 to 15 years. Announced in Seoul today, the strategy brings together the institution’s public and private sector capabilities to help developing economies expand digital connectivity, improve access to technology and create employment opportunities. World Bank Group President Ajay Banga said the initiative would focus on practical applications of technology, particularly affordable artificial intelligence tools that can improve productivity and public services. The strategy identifies digital technology as a means of improving productivity and expanding employment in infrastructure, energy, agriculture, healthcare, tourism and manufacturing. The World Bank said more than two billion people remained offline globally in 2025.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the FDI Policy.India’s foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade, with the government liberalising sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the country. The government has progressively liberalised FDI norms in key sectors, including defence, telecommunications, insurance and space. Foreign investment of up to 74 per cent is permitted in defence, 100 per cent in telecom, insurance and Space sector. The country has received a record over 748 billion US dollars in FDI between 2014 and 2025. The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112. Addressing the Rozgar Mela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than one hundred countries are investing in India through FDI.Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran said that India has opened up several sectors, including space, drones, defence and insurance, to foreign investment.The FDI policy reforms reflect India’s efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment, simplified investment procedures and to strengthen its position as a preferred global investment destination.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Union Home Minister Amit Shah today paid tribute to former Vice President of India Bhairon Singh Shekhawat on his birth anniversary.In a social media post, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that Mr Shekhawat’s life was an inspiring saga of struggle, public service and unwavering commitment to ethical values. He highlighted Mr Shekhawat’s close connection with the masses and his dedication to integrity, honesty and transparency. The Defence Minister said that Mr Shekhawat’s contributions to the development of the country, particularly Rajasthan, will always be remembered.In a separate social media post, Union Home Minister Amit Shah described Mr Shekhawat as a skilled organiser. He said that as Chief Minister of Rajasthan, Mr Shekhawat worked to ensure the implementation of public welfare measures and strengthen the organisation in the state. Mr Shah added that Mr Shekhawat demonstrated how dedication and hard work can help achieve every goal. He said that Mr Shekhawat’s life, marked by simplicity, integrity and empathy, remains an inexhaustible source of inspiration for every social worker.

. In French Open Badminton Tournament, Indian shuttlers PV Sindhu and Ashmita Chaliha have advanced to the Women’s Singles Quarter-finals after straight-game victories. Unseeded Ashmita registered the biggest upset of the day, defeating world number two and third seed Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 21-19, 21-18 in 37 minutes. Sindhu also secured a comfortable win, beating Japan’s Riko Gunji 21-12, 21-16 in 44 minutes to enter the last eight.In Quarter finals today, Ashmita will take on Japan’s Nozomi Okuhara, while PV Sindhu will take on Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-Chian.However, India’s Tanvi Sharma and Ayush Shetty bowed out in the pre-quarter-finals. Tanvi lost to world number one An Se Young of South Korea, while Ayush retired hurt against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka in the Men’s Singles.

. The United Nations Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage has approved 20 million US dollars to support Nepal’s recovery from the devastating floods in August. The decision was taken at an extraordinary meeting of the Fund’s Board yesterday, following an urgent request from Nepal.An ice-and-rock avalanche in the Himalayas on 26th August this year triggered floods along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, destroying homes, roads, hydropower projects and other critical infrastructure. A government assessment estimates damage and economic losses at 2.7 billion US dollars, while recovery and reconstruction will require around 4.7 billion dollars. The proposed 20-million-dollar assistance will contribute to these efforts.The assistance has not yet been disbursed. Nepal is required to submit a detailed project proposal for approval by the Fund, which supports vulnerable developing countries in addressing the impacts of climate change.

. India’s double Olympic medallist P V Sindhu survived a scare from Thailand’s world No. 26 Supanida Katethong to advance in the French Open Super 750 badminton tournament in Paris yesterday. The former world champion and world No. 1 battled for an hour and four minutes before prevailing 21-14, 8-21, 23-21 in a gruelling encounter.Sindhu started strongly, taking the opening game 21-14, but Katethong fought back in the second, dominating the rallies to level the match with a commanding 21-8 win. The decider proved to be a tense affair, with both players fighting for every point. Sindhu eventually held her nerve in the closing stages to edge past the Thai shuttler 23-21 and seal her place in the next round. The next clash is scheduled for today.

. India has said that the United Nations is losing its legitimacy as the outcome of a war fought eight decades ago continues to shape the composition of the UN Security Council. India has called for reforms to make the Council more representative and reflective of contemporary global realities.Addressing the UN General Assembly yesterday, India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, P. Harish, said that no war fought over 80 years ago should determine the present-day world order. He said the authority derived from victory in the Second World War could not compensate for the lack of legitimacy arising from an unrepresentative Security Council.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined over 8.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 726 billion US dollars during the week ended 9th of October. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 7.1 billion dollars to 597.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 1.3 billion dollars to 105 billion dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 109 million dollars to 18.5 billion dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 10 million dollars to 4.78 billion dollars.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar on winning Gold in the Para Compound Mixed Team event at the Asian Para Games 2026. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that their superb victory was a wonderful display of skill, composure and teamwork.Mr Modi also congratulated Suvarna Raj on her magnificent victory in the Women’s Discus Throw F54 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that her success is the result of her hard work, perseverance and unwavering commitment to sporting excellence. He said that India celebrates this wonderful triumph.The Prime Minister has also congratulated Anjanaben on winning Gold in the Women’s 400m T47 event with an outstanding timing. Mr Modi said that her exceptional speed, focus and determination have brought great joy to the nation.Mr Modi has congratulated Shailesh Kumar for winning Gold with an impressive jump and setting a new Games Record in the Men’s High Jump T42/T63 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. He said that this is a remarkable accomplishment that reflects his talent, consistency and dedication.The Prime Minister also congratulated Swati Chaudhary for creating history by winning India’s first-ever medal in Women’s W1 Archery at the Asian Para Games, bringing home a Silver on her debut. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that her determination is truly commendable and wished that she continues to make the nation proud.Mr Modi also congratulated Kapil Kumar for securing Silver Medal in the Men’s 400m Freestyle S10 event, clocking an impressive timing. The Prime Minister said that his endurance, dedication and determination have earned him a well-deserved place on the podium.The Prime Minister has congratulated Tejalben Damor for winning Silver in the Women’s 400m T12 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. Mr Modi said that her speed, determination and commitment to excellence are truly commendable.Mr Modi also congratulated Jayanti for winning a Silver Medal in the Women’s 400m T47 event at the Asian Para Games 2026.The Prime Minister has commended the efforts of Pramod Bhagat and Manisha Ramadass as the duo secured Bronze in the Mixed Doubles SL3-SU5 Para Badminton event at the Asian Para Games 2026. The Prime Minister said that their teamwork, determination and competitive spirit have been evident throughout the tournament. Complimenting both athletes for their performance, he wished them for their future endeavours.The Prime Minister also congratulated Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan and Krishna Nagar on winning the Bronze Medal in the Mixed Doubles SH6 Para Badminton event at the Games. Mr Modi said that their dedication has brought another proud moment for Indian Para Badminton and wished them continued success in the competitions ahead.Mr Modi also said that Suhas L. Yathiraj continues to distinguish himself on the international sporting stage. He has won the Bronze in the Men’s Singles SL4 Para Badminton event at the Asian Para Games 2026. The Prime Minister said that his consistency, perseverance and passion for the sport are truly admirable.The Prime Minister also congratulated Bhavina Patel and Shubham Wadhwa on winning Bronze in the Mixed Doubles Class XD7 event, securing India’s first-ever medal in Mixed Doubles at the Games. Mr Modi said that their teamwork, dedication and determination have brought pride to the nation.Congratulating Abhijeet Sakhuja for winning the Bronze in the Men’s Singles SL4 Para Badminton event, Mr Modi wished him a bright future in the sport. The Prime Minister said that reaching the podium in his first appearance is a commendable achievement and reflects his talent, dedication and hard work.The Prime Minister has also congratulated Sanjana Kumari for winning a Bronze Medal in the Women’s Singles SL3 Para Badminton event at the Asian Para Games.Mr Modi has also congratulated Manisha Ramadass on winning Bronze in the Women’s Singles SU5 Para Badminton event. The Prime Minister said that securing a Bronze Medal for the second consecutive edition reflects her consistency and commitment to the sport. He added, her efforts and competitive spirit are truly commendable and wished that she continue to achieve greater success in the years ahead.The Prime Minister also congratulated Naveen Sivakumar and Surya Kant Yadav for securing India’s first-ever medal in the Men’s Doubles SL3-SU5 category at the Asian Para Games 2026. Mr Modi said that this achievement on their debut is a special milestone for both athletes. He added, their teamwork, perseverance and dedication deserve appreciation.Mr Modi also greeted Rahul for securing Bronze Medal in the Men’s High Jump T42/T63 event with a fine jump. He wished that the athlete continue to reach new heights in the times to come.The Prime Minister also commended Ravi Karthik Budigina for winning Bronze medal in the Men’s 50m Freestyle S13 event. He said that the athlete’s passion and commitment are noteworthy.

Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets demanding free elections and political reforms amid uncertainty over the country’s political future.Yesterday, the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years was held in Caracas and several other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo. Security forces maintained a limited presence at protest sites, while demonstrators in several smaller cities dispersed before dark. The protests come months after US forces captured former President Nicolas Maduro in January. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez, Maduro’s former deputy, is now leading the country’s government with US backing.Both Rodriguez and US President Donald Trump have expressed support for holding elections but have yet to announce dates for legislative or presidential polls. Machado has called for elections to be held by July 2027.Machado, who received the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, has been outside Venezuela for nearly a year after going into hiding following the disputed 2024 election. Opposition vote tallies indicated that her candidate won the presidential contest, but Maduro’s government rejected the claim and never released complete official results.Meanwhile, US-backed negotiations between opposition factions and the interim government are focusing on reforms to the Supreme Court and electoral council to improve the fairness of future elections.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

. In Tibet, 16 people have been killed and over 54 injured after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City last evening. Hundreds of homes collapsed and rockfalls were trigerred. Rescue operations are underway with more than 1,600 personnel deployed to assist those affected and provide emergency relief.The Nagqu media office said, at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed in the earthquake. Of the 46 injured, 11 were in serious condition. Communication services were disrupted in parts of the region, while railway authorities halted train services as a precaution.Meanwhile, Intermittent snowfall is forecast in the affected region over the next three days, raising concerns for residents displaced by the earthquake and those involved in rescue operations.India’s National Centre for Seismology said the earthquake struck Nagqu City at 8:03 PM Indian Standard Time, at a depth of 173 kilometres, around 400 kilometres from Lhasa.

. Bringing festive cheer to Dalal Street, both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will host the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session on November 8 this year. According to the circular released by the exchanges, the markets will open at 2:20 PM and close at 3:30 PM. The Muhurat trading marks the auspicious beginning of the new Samvat year, as investors make their symbolic trades for prosperity and good fortune. All trades executed during this session will carry normal settlement obligations.

At the Asian Para Games, India clinched three gold medals, with Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi winning the men’s recurve doubles archery event, Nitesh Kumar claiming gold in the men’s singles SL3 para-badminton event and Naveen Sivakumar clinches gold in the men’s singles SL4 final.India also secured four silver medals across para-athletics, para-archery and para-badminton.In para-athletics, Parmod won silver in the men’s 1,500-metre T46 event, clocking 4 minutes 9.65 seconds to finish second. He retained the silver medal he had won at the Hangzhou edition three years ago.In para-archery, Bhawna and Pooja won silver in the women’s recurve doubles event after losing 0-6 to China in the gold-medal match. Nimisha Chakkungalparambil wins silver in the women’s long jump T47 with a best effort of 5.37m.Meanwhile, in para-badminton, Thulasimathi Murugesan claimed silver in the women’s singles SU5 event. She lost to China’s Qiuxia Yang 18-21, 11-21 in the final.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has warned that the European Union’s carbon tax on steel and other industrial products could raise infrastructure costs, fuel inflation and weaken the bloc’s global competitiveness.Addressing the Berlin Global Dialogue yesterday, Mr Goyal criticised the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), warning that higher costs of steel, aluminium and cement could increase infrastructure expenditure and affect European businesses and consumers. He also cautioned that growing regulatory restrictions could create trade barriers and trigger retaliatory measures from trading partners.Mr Goyal also criticised developed nations for failing to fulfil their commitment to mobilise 100 billion dollars annually in climate finance for developing countries. He highlighted that India accounts for around 17 per cent of the global population but less than 3 per cent of global carbon emissions, while pursuing one of the world’s fastest-growing clean energy programmes. He called for climate policies that recognise the differing responsibilities of developed and developing countries and support India’s efforts to meet its development needs while expanding clean energy and greener steel production.Earlier, at the India-Germany Business Roundtable in Berlin, Mr Goyal called for increasing bilateral trade from around 31.5 billion euros to 310 billion euros, stressing cooperation in manufacturing, investment and technology. He highlighted opportunities in precision engineering, digital technologies, infrastructure and skill development, and said the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement could create fresh business opportunities.The Minister urged businesses to prepare for the agreement’s implementation by identifying potential customers, investors and partners. Mr Goyal is on an official visit to Germany until tomorrow and will travel to the Netherlands from tomorrow to Thursday to strengthen trade, investment and technological cooperation.

. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for restraint amid escalating hostilities in Yemen. He condemned Houthi attacks on civilian targets in Saudi Arabia, warning that the violence is increasing civilian suffering and regional tensions.In a post on social media, Mr Guterres called for a political solution to the conflict, saying the continued hostilities were inflicting immense suffering on civilians.Meanwhile, Yemen’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs welcomed a European Parliament resolution urging the European Union to designate the Houthi movement as a terrorist organisation. The ministry described the move as an important step towards protecting civilians, strengthening regional security and ensuring the safety of international navigation.In its resolution, adopted yesterday, the European Parliament condemned Houthi attacks as violations of international law and international humanitarian law. It also expressed concern over civilian casualties, displacement and the worsening humanitarian crisis in Yemen, while condemning Houthi missile and drone attacks against Israel and the United Arab Emirates in recent years.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 46 paise to close at 94 rupees and 47 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.68 in intra-day trade.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. According to IMD, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience heavy rainfall today.MetDepartment has also predicted thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over East Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Lakshadweep, Madhya Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh today. Similar weather conditions are likely to prevail over Odisha, Rayalaseema, Telangana, Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka for the day.For Delhi, the Weather Agency has forecast a clear sky today.

. Heavy rain is expected to continue at isolated places across all districts of Keralam today. Orange alert has been issued in nine districts. The orange alert, indicating isolated very heavy rainfall, is in force in Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts. Yellow alert, indicating isolated heavy rainfall, has been issued in the remaining districts. Rainfall is likely to further intensify tomorrow, with orange alert issued in ten districts.On Sunday, eleven districts will be under orange alert. Although the intensity of rainfall is expected to decrease slightly on Monday, yellow alert has been issued for all fourteen districts. Meanwhile, orange alert will remain in force in Lakshadweep today and tomorrow.

. Domestic investors are set to navigate a week packed with key market drivers, including macroeconomic data, corporate earnings results, and geopolitical developments. Market sentiment will also be driven by foreign institutional investor (FII) flows, commodity prices, bond yield movements, and currency fluctuations during the holiday-shortened week ahead.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Dussehra. Market participants will closely track the country’s core industries growth figures and forex reserves data. On the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are set to open for subscription, including one of the biggest IPOs in India so far.Globally, investors will closely monitor developments surrounding the West Asia conflict. Bank of South Korea is scheduled to declare its monetary policy decision. In Japan, inflation data will be on focus along with an eye on China’s third quarter GDP estimates and industrial production data.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi today. Mr Modi will also address the gathering on the occasion.The three-day event marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all.Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service. The event will bring together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad.  The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister Modi releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita, produced by Chinmaya Mission in Tamil Nadu.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism, and decades after Independence. Over the past few years, the Government has slowly been steering India, away from these vestiges of British rule. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence Day in 2022, the Prime Minister outlined five resolutions, or Panch Pran for the next 25 years. Elaborating on the second Praan, he said, in no part of citizens’ existence, not even in the deepest corners of mind or habits should there be any ounce of slavery.In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct Indian identity, the Government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors. the historic Rajpath in New Delhi was renamed Kartavya Path and inaugurated by the Prime Minister in 2022.  Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed near India Gate, which has replaced the statue of King George the Fifth. The Indian Navy also adopted a new ensign in 2022, replacing the earlier design that featured the Saint George’s Cross. The Government has merged the Rail Budget with the Union Budget from budget year 2017-18, ending a practice dating back to 1924. BJP leader Ram Madhav has said that restoring India’s cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added that decolonisation is the real patriotism that is happening today.The Government has further sought to revive literature banned during British rule, with the National Archives of India compiling a catalogue of banned poems, writings and publications from the freedom struggle. In addition, more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify governance and remove outdated legal provisions.These initiatives reflect the Government’s stated commitment to building a confident, self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.

Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IITM) Pravartak has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Sri Lanka’s telecom giant Dialogue Axiata PLC to jointly support the country’s research and innovation ecosystem. IITM Pravartak is a technology innovation hub funded by India’s Department of Science and Technology.The collaboration aims to connect universities and startups with technological expertise, business support and access to markets in Sri Lanka and beyond. The agreement was signed by Dr. M. J. Shankar Raman, CEO of IITM Pravartak, and Supun Weerasinghe, Group CEO of Dialogue Axiata PLC, in the presence of the Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, Santosh Jha.Explaining the focus of the partnership, Dr Raman said the collaboration would work with universities and startups to develop ideas that address business needs and provide the technological support required to take them forward.The agreement will strengthen deep tech and innovation partnership between India and Sri Lanka.

. The United States will introduce a new requirement for all US-bound air passengers to declare whether they have visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in the previous 21 days as part of measures to prevent the spread of Ebola.According to a new order issued by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the requirement will take effect on November 3. Passengers will be required to submit declarations either digitally or on paper.The CDC is scheduled to brief major US and international airlines on the new requirements and compliance procedures. The measures come amid an ongoing outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in Africa. The CDC has also imposed restrictions on foreign nationals who have visited Uganda or South Sudan in the previous three weeks. The CDC has said that no cases linked to the current outbreak have been reported in the United States.

. Baloch American Congress (BAC) President Tara Chand Baloch urged the international community to intervene and stop the forced displacement of Baloch families from Kalat district of Balochistan by Pakistani authorities.Citing reports, Tara Chand yesterday said that Pakistani forces and authorities have been forcing Baloch families to abandon their ancestral homes and villages in the Kalat Shor Parod region. The BAC President stressed that Baloch people deserve to live in peace, dignity, and safety on their ancestral land, and the world must not remain silent when innocent families are suffering.His statement comes after the Balochistan government ordered around 5,000 families in Kalat’s Shoor Paarod area to vacate their homes by October 30 and warned that people who refuse to leave will be removed by force. As many as 30,000 people living in the mountainous area will be impacted by the relocation plan approved by Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti.

. India’s para archers Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar clinched the compound mixed team gold at the Asian Para Games, beating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in a one-sided final in Aichi-Nagoya today. The top-seeded Indians, who set a new world record in the qualification round, consistently hit the target to build and maintain their lead throughout the clash.India edged ahead 38-37 in the opening end before extending their advantage to four points at 77-73 in the second, dropping just one point in the process. Earlier, Suvarna Raj bagged a gold medal by winning the women’s F-54 discus throw event. In para-archery, Swati Chaudhary secured silver in the women’s W-1 category.In para table tennis, Bhavina Patel and Shubham Wadhwa confirmed a medal in mixed doubles XD7 after defeating Japan’s Kimie Bessho and Masanori Uno in straight games, 11-9, 11-3, and 11-6. They will face a South Korean pair in the semifinals. Meanwhile, Dattaprasad Chougule and Savita lost 2-3 to the Philippines in the XD17 quarterfinals despite winning the first two games.India also secured several bronze medals in para-badminton. Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat lost their mixed doubles semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani. Sanjana Kumari won bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja secured bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also claimed bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

. India continued its impressive performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the country bagged 26 medals including 7 Gold, 4 Silver and 15 Bronze today. With this, India’s medal tally has risen to 88, including 21 Gold, 26 Silver and 41 Bronze. India is currently in 4th position in the medal tally.India swept the men’s high jump T63 event today with Shailesh Kumar winning Gold, Varun Bhati bagging silver and Rahul securing bronze.Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record to clinch gold in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump combined event, successfully defending his title at the Asian Para Games. Dharmaraj set a new Asian record with a winning jump of 7.15 metres.Sprinter Anjanaben Bumbadiya struck gold in the women’s 400 metre T47 event. Bumbadiya clinched the gold with a time of 59.97 seconds and was followed by compatriot Jayanti Behera in second place.  In the women’s 400m T12 event, visually impaired Tejalben Damor won her second medal of the Games by finishing with a silver after clocking 57.60 seconds. Dilip Mahadu Gavit won the gold medal in men’s 400 metre T47 race, clocking 48.27 seconds.Suvarna Raj clinched a gold medal in the women’s F54 discus throw with a best effort of 15.66 metres.Armless archer Sheetal Devi reigned supreme in the women’s compound individual and mixed team events to claim gold in both competitions. She overcame a four-point deficit to defeat Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in a repeat of the Hangzhou 2023 final.Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar bagged gold in the Archery compound mixed team event, defeating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in the final.Swati Chaudhary created history by winning India’s first-ever medal in the W-1 category, securing silver in the women’s individual event. She lost 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan in the final despite taking an early 4-2 lead.Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa got a bronze medal in the mixed doubles XD7 Table Tennis competition.Kapil Kumar clinched the silver while Swatik Patil bagged the bronze medal in their respective swimming events.India also added several bronze medals in para-Badminton.Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat claimed bronze in mixed doubles after losing their semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani.Sanjana Kumari secured bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja bagged bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also got bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

The African Union and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention have called for enhanced solidarity and coordinated action to contain the spreading Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak across Africa.The call came after AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf and Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya discussed continental response and preparedness measures yesterday.Kaseya stressed the need for transparency, timely decisions and urgent mobilisation of resources to contain the outbreak and strengthen public health preparedness. The outbreak has spread across three African regions, with confirmed cases reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Africa CDC is scheduled to convene an emergency ministerial meeting next Wednesday, bringing together ministers of health, finance and transport to strengthen the continent’s collective response.

. Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense (MND) has detected three Chinese naval vessels and seven official ships operating around the island in the morning. In social media post, the Ministry said the Republic of China (ROC) Armed Forces had closely monitored the maritime activities and deployed appropriate assets in response to the situation. The ministry also stated that no Chinese military aircraft were detected operating around Taiwan during the 24-hour monitoring period. Consequently, no flight path illustration was provided in the latest update.Earlier on Monday, Taiwan’s defence ministry reported detecting five sorties of Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels and nine official ships operating around the island until 6 AM local time. It said three of the five aircraft sorties crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait and entered Taiwan’s northern, central and southwestern Air Defence Identification Zone (ADIZ).

India and Uzbekistan today agreed to cooperate in addressing the threats and challenges to national and regional security, and further strengthen the framework of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism. The tenth meeting of India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism was held in New Delhi.The two sides discussed the threats posed by terrorist groups globally and in their respective regions. Both sides exchanged views on current and emerging challenges to counter-terrorism. These include countering extremism and radicalization, combating financing of terrorism, preventing use of technology for terrorist purposes, and the nexus between transnational organized crime and terrorism.External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the two sides also deliberated on the measures to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the sphere of counter terrorism through information sharing, capacity building and sharing of best practices. They discussed the prospects of developing cooperation in the fight against terrorism between the relevant agencies of India and Uzbekistan. Both sides reaffirmed commitment to strengthen cooperation in multilateral fora including the UN, SCO-RATS and EAG.The meeting was co-chaired by Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism), Ministry of External Affairs, Dr. Suhel Ajaz Khan and Head of the Department for Cooperation with South Asian, Near, Middle Eastern and African Countries under Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pirimkulov Gulomjon Shodmonkulovich.

This landmark legislation reserves one-third of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. World Health Organisation-WHO has reported the first documented human infection with the Shamonda virus in France after an immuno compromised patient died following the infection.WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has said, the virus was previously detected only in animals, including cattle, sheep, goats, and horses. The virus is believed to spread among animals through the bites of midges, small fly-like insects. However, further studies are needed to establish how the infection was transmitted to the patient and to assess potential public health risks.Meanwhile, Nigeria has confirmed an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja. Health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring.

. Taiwan is largely shut down today as Typhoon Champi is approaching the island, threatening strong winds and severe rain. Although the storm has weakened and is not expected to make direct landfall, authorities have warned that its impact could be felt across much of the island for nearly two days.According to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA), Champi is packing wind gusts of around 191 kilometres per hour near its centre and is located about 330 kilometres east of Taiwan’s southern tip. The storm’s circulation extends approximately 320 kilometres, potentially affecting most of the island.As a precautionary measure, Taiwan’s financial markets, schools and government offices have been closed across much of the island. The Transport Ministry has also announced the cancellation of all 262 domestic flights scheduled for today, along with more than 350 international flights.The CWA has forecast that Champi will pass just off northeastern Taiwan before turning north towards the Chinese coast and eventually moving towards southern Japan. The typhoon is also expected to pass over Yonaguni, Japan’s westernmost inhabited island in Okinawa Prefecture.

. President Droupadi Murmu will visit Jagdalpur in Chhattisgarh on the second day of her visit to the state today. She will attend key events, including the historic Muria Durbar as part of the famous Bastar Dussehra celebrations.Akashvani Correspondent reports that the President will reach Jagdalpur airport this morning. Her first stop will be the historic Maa Danteshwari Temple, where she will offer prayers.Later, President Murmu will attend the historic Muria Durbar. Dating back to Bastar’s royal era, this gathering serves as a bridge between traditional community leaders-such as Manjhis and Chalkis-and government officials to address local issues. Later, at the Lalbagh Maidan, the President will interact with local tribal leaders, priests, and residents before departing for Delhi.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that a new world order is emerging, as the old world order is unable to address the challenges facing the world. He said India will play a key role in this new world order and called for the collective well-being of humankind.Delivering the keynote address on ‘A World Between Orders’ at a summit in New Delhi last evening, the Prime Minister said the advent of technology has given rise to new powers and new voices. He said India is strengthening its own capabilities to help strengthen the world.The Prime Minister also stressed the need for reforms in multilateral organisations. He added that the voice of the Global South deserves its due place. He stated that international cooperation should not be limited to good times, but remain effective during crises.The Prime Minister stated that India is working towards becoming one of the world’s three largest economies and said that, despite global uncertainties, India has emerged as the world’s fastest-growing major economy. He put forth the vision of “Power to Empower”, saying Viksit Bharat is not just about India’s own progress but also a guarantee of a better world. Mr Modi said that as India moves towards self-reliance, it strengthens global supply chains. He stated that India is now collaborating with the world not merely as a back office, but as a brain office. Pointing out that India hosts over half of the world’s Global Capability Centres, the Prime Minister explained that these hubs have pivoted from basic support services to advanced AI, cloud computing, engineering, analytics and product development.Mr Modi cautioned that while the world is searching for a new order, some people are dreaming of disorder in India. He said the image of a strong India should be known globally at a time when there is so much chaos in the world. He said some people are trying to malign India’s reputation. Taking a dig at Congress, Mr Modi said some people go abroad and defame India.At the same event, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that, in many cases of unrest worldwide, there has been external encouragement and support from people who see such situations as a tool to advance their agenda. Replying to a question, Dr Jaishankar remarked that turbulence and volatility have continuously increased as the world has changed, borderless politics has grown, technology has spread and the world economy has become globalised.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav has said, the Government has progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams. He said that these streams include plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, and others.Addressing the Circular Economy Conference in New Delhi yesterday, the Minister said, these rules are focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. He highlighted that as on date, that around 500 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams.On plastic waste management, the Minister called for greater coordination between producers and recyclers to address concerns over the availability of recyclable material and recycling capacity. He further called for stronger recovery of critical minerals from e-waste and batteries, and greater industry participation in developing secondary raw-material markets and strengthening supply-chain traceability.
